title: Searching for a record in a file

visuals.title: Searching a file: read, compare, remember

stages.name: 1. Open and set found = false
stages.detail: Open the file, check it, and prepare the flag found = false (and matches = 0 if you count).

stages.name: 2. Read one record
stages.detail: while (in >> roll >> name >> marks): one complete record is read each round.

stages.name: 3. Compare with the key
stages.detail: if (roll == key). For names use name == key. If equal: use the record, set found = true, (break if the id is unique).

stages.name: 4. End of file
stages.detail: If the loop ends without a match, found is still false.

stages.name: 5. Report
stages.detail: if (!found) print "Record not found". Close the file.

visuals.title: Match each searching idea to its meaning

pairs.meaning: A flag that remembers if a match was seen
Compare the record just read with the wanted value
Stop reading as soon as a unique record is found
Count every record that matches (no break)
Runs AFTER the loop to print Record not found
Update a record: read all into an array, change one, write all back

goal: After this you can search a file for a record by id or name, count the matches, print "not found", and update a record by loading the file into an array and saving it again.
warmup: You look for your friend's name on the exam result sheet pinned on the notice board. You read the list from the top, one name after another. When you see your friend's name you stop and read the marks. If you reach the end of the list and never saw the name, you say "he is not on the list". That is exactly a file search: read, compare, stop when found, report if not.
definition: A text file has no index, so searching means reading the records from the start and comparing each one with the key (the value you look for). A Boolean flag found starts as false and becomes true when a record matches. After the loop, if found is still false, print "Record not found". If the key is unique (a roll number) you can break at the first match. If many records can match (a name) do not break: count them with a counter instead. To update or delete a record in a text file you cannot change one line in place. The simple method is: load all records into an array, change the array, and write the whole array back to the file with a plain ofstream.
howItWorks: Follow the first trace: the loop reads record by record, compares roll with key and stops at 103. The check if (!found) comes after the loop, never inside it: inside the loop it would print "not found" for every record that does not match (see the first mistake). The second example searches by name and counts every match, so it must not break. The function returns the count, and main prints "not found" when it is 0. The third example is the standard way to save and load an array of structures: saveAll writes one line per record, loadAll reads them back with while (n < maxSize && in >> ...) so the array can never overflow. To update a record, loadAll, change the array element, then saveAll: the plain ofstream erases the old file and writes the new, correct content. (Another technique is to write the changed records to a temporary file and then delete the old file and rename the new one. Our notes do not use remove and rename, so we only mention it here.) Never open the same file with ofstream while you still want to read its old content: opening for writing erases it at once.

worked.problem: Exam question: Save an array of 3 students into students.txt. Load the file into another array, change the marks of roll 102 to 95, save the array back to the file, load it again and display every record.
pseudocode: SAVE the first array (3 records) to students.txt
LOAD the file into array list, n = number of records
FOR each record: IF roll = 102 THEN marks = 95, found = true
IF found THEN SAVE list back ELSE PRINT not found
LOAD the file again into array check
FOR each record in check: PRINT it

  D --> E{i less than n?}
  E -- Yes --> F{roll equals key?}
  F -- Yes --> G[Change marks, found = true]
  F -- No --> H[i = i + 1]
  G --> H
  H --> E
  E -- No --> I{found?}
  I -- Yes --> J[Save list back to the file]
  I -- No --> K[/Print not found/]
  J --> L[Load again and print all]
  K --> L
  L --> M([End])

Reads records into the array and returns how many were read.
The n < maxSize test stops us before the array is full. Then a whole record is read into s[n].

Search in the ARRAY now, not in the file.

mistakes.error: No compiler error. We ran it on the file 101 and 102 with key 102 and it printed: Not found / Found Sana /. The message Not found appears for every record that does not match. Use a flag and test it after the loop.

mistakes.wrong:
ofstream upd("s.txt", ios::app);
upd << "101 Ali 90" << endl;   // 'updating' marks
mistakes.right: // load all records into an array, change the array, saveAll() with a plain ofstream
mistakes.error: No compiler error. Appending does not change the old line: the file now has the old record and the new one. We counted: 2 lines for one student. To update, rewrite the whole file.

mistakes.right: // first load the records, THEN open ofstream and save
mistakes.error: No compiler error. Opening an ofstream erases the file immediately, so the reader finds nothing. We ran it and got: 0 records. Read everything first, write after.
No compiler error. matches was never given a start value, so the count begins from a garbage number. Always start counters and flags at 0 / false.
The program compiles but is wrong: a single = assigns key to roll, so the condition is true whenever key is not 0. Use == to compare.

examTips: Draw the search pattern: found = false; loop reading records; if equal then print, found = true, break; after the loop if (!found) print not found.
Use break only when the key is unique. If the question says "count" or "all students named...", do not break.
Put "Record not found" AFTER the loop, never inside it.
To update a record in a text file: load into an array, change, write all back. Mention that ios::app only adds at the end.
Never open an ofstream on the file you still want to read: it erases the content.
romanSummary: File mein search ke liye shuru se har record parho aur key se compare karo. Mil jaye to found = true karo aur (agar key unique hai) break karo.
Loop ke BAAD if (!found) likh kar "Record not found" print karein, loop ke andar nahi.
Agar naam kai baar aa sakta hai to break na karein, matches++ se ginti karein.
Record update karne ke liye saara data array mein load karein, array mein change karein, phir poori file dobara ofstream se likh dein.
ios::app sirf naya record aakhir mein jorne ke liye hai, purana record badalne ke liye nahi.

quiz.prompt: Where should if (!found) cout << "Record not found"; be placed?
quiz.hint: Decide only when all records were seen.
quiz.explanation: Inside the loop it would print for every non-matching record.

quiz.prompt: When can you use break in a file search?
options: When the key is unique, such as a roll number
quiz.answer: When the key is unique, such as a roll number
quiz.explanation: With a unique key there is nothing more to find.

quiz.prompt: How do you update one student's marks in a text file?
options: Load all records into an array, change it, write all back
Open with ios::app and write the new marks
quiz.answer: Load all records into an array, change it, write all back
quiz.hint: A text file cannot change one line in place.
quiz.explanation: Appending only adds a second record; rewriting replaces the file.

quiz.prompt: What happens if you open ofstream on a file and then try to read its old content?
options: The old content is already erased
The file is deleted from the disk only after the program ends
quiz.answer: The old content is already erased
quiz.hint: Plain ofstream erases at open time.

quiz.prompt: Searching a file for a name that can appear many times needs...
options: a break at the first match
quiz.explanation: matches++ for each hit, and the loop runs to the end of the file.
